analysis.investment_thesis: FACT trades at a P/E of 3,944x and P/B of 42.48x — multiples that defy any rational valuation framework — while reporting negative operating margins (-3.28%) and net profit that has collapsed 93% in two years (INR 613 Cr → 41 Cr). This is a government-backed PSU kept alive by state patronage, not by business merit, and the market price reflects speculation entirely disconnected from earning power.
key_strengths: Government of India promoter (90% stake) — existential risk is low, state will not allow outright default
Revenue CAGR of 9.8% over nine years demonstrates some scale-building capacity
Operating cash flow positive in all 5 of last 5 years, though rapidly eroding (INR 638 Cr → 140 Cr)
key_risks: Valuation is grotesque — P/B of 42.48x for a business with 1.61% ROE destroys any margin of safety
Borrowings nearly doubled in a single year (INR 1,810 Cr in 2024 → 3,837 Cr in 2025) while FCF turned negative (-13 Cr)
Earnings are structurally deteriorating: operating margin is now negative (-3.28%) and net profit of INR 41 Cr on INR 4,051 Cr revenue is essentially zero
red_flags: P/E of 3,944x — one of the most extreme overvaluations a Graham analyst could encounter
Debt/Equity of 2.79x vs. Graham's maximum of 0.5x; borrowings surged 112% in FY2025 alone
Equity was negative as recently as FY2021 (-INR 180 Cr) — this company was technically insolvent within memory
Net profit collapsed from INR 613 Cr (2023) to INR 41 Cr (2025) — a 93% decline in two years
Operating margin negative at -3.28% — the core business is currently losing money before interest and taxes
analysis.detailed_analysis:
FACT fails every single quantitative filter I have established over decades of analysis. The Graham Number requires price below sqrt(22.5 × EPS × BVPS); with a P/E of 3,944x and P/B of 42.48x, the stock trades at roughly 280x the Graham Number — a figure so absurd it warrants no further discussion. The company's ROE of 1.61% means shareholders earned roughly nothing on the INR 1,375 Cr of equity in FY2025, while the market demands a INR 58,414 Cr capitalisation for that privilege. Debt/Equity at 2.79x obliterates my 0.5x ceiling, and the FY2025 borrowings surge (INR 1,810 → 3,837 Cr) while free cash flow turned negative is a textbook sign of a business consuming capital without generating returns.

The earnings history is neither stable nor dependable — the company reported losses in FY2016, FY2017, and FY2018, and after a brief profitable run (FY2019–FY2023), profits have collapsed nearly to zero again. Mr. Market appears to be pricing in a government rescue, a subsidy windfall, or some speculative catalyst. None of these belong in the calculation of intrinsic value. The intelligent investor demands a margin of safety; here there is none — the stock price is the risk. I would not purchase this security at any price remotely near current levels.
